chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who is taught a surah from the decisive (obligatory) ones, and it is repeated upon him multiple times in one sitting (standing position). He said: 'He must prostrate every time he hears it, and the one who teaches him must also prostrate.'

key_terms.السُّورَةَ مِنَ الْعَزَائِمِ: An obligatory Quranic surah (e.g., Al-Asr, Al-Kawthar) whose recitation is required in prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prostration when a surah is repeated multiple times while being taught during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific ruling for *sajdah al-tilawah* when a learner is being instructed on an obligatory surah, mandating prostration for both parties upon each hearing. It highlights the scholarly principle that the act of listening to the recitation of a verse of prostration triggers the obligation, even in an instructional setting within a single prayer session. This ruling underscores the communal and reciprocal nature of Quranic recitation in Shia jurisprudence.
